# 1 Clement Chapter 34 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 34 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_034_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 34

**34:1** The good worker collects his pay with confidence; but the lazy, negligent worker can't even look his employer in the eye.

**34:2** So we must be eager in doing good — for everything comes from him.

**34:3** He gives us this advance notice: "Look, the Lord is coming, and his reward is with him, to pay each one according to his work."

**34:4** So he is calling those who believe in him with their whole heart to be diligent and active in every good work.

**34:5** Let him be our pride and our confidence. Let us submit to his will. Let us contemplate the vast army of his angels, how they stand at the ready and carry out his will.

**34:6** For scripture says: "Ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him, and thousands of thousands served him, and they cried out: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts; all creation is full of his glory."

**34:7** So let us too, united in one mind and conscience, cry out to him eagerly as with one voice, so that we may share in his great and glorious promises.

**34:8** For it says: "No eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has imagined the things that God has prepared for those who wait for him."

---

*PNEUMA renders the Trisagion (v. 6) and the Isaiah 64:4 citation (v. 8) with the resonance they have in Christian liturgical tradition, while making the surrounding argument immediately accessible.*
